outlook.statement: Focus going forward will remain clear and consistent: to strengthen core businesses, maintain highest standards of quality and compliance, improve efficiency through better processes and thoughtful use of technology and build capabilities that support sustainable growth.

The Company has embarked on a series of strategic and operational measures that is expected to result in improvement in the performance of the Company. It has been aggressively pursuing and implementing its strategies to improve financial performance.
Your Directors are also striving to achieve further growth in sales and better financial performance in the forthcoming years.

Albert David Limited will continue to strengthen its R&D capabilities with a focus on placenta-based therapies, novel drug delivery systems, conventional drug delivery systems and neglected tropical diseases. The Company aims to expand its global footprint by pursuing patents for innovative Placentrex-based products, thereby achieving international recognition.

Future priorities include scaling up collaborations with premier research institutions and global partners, accelerating development of next-generation formulations, leveraging advanced manufacturing technologies to improve efficiency and sustainability, expanding regulatory submissions to new geographies, and exploring novel indications and delivery routes for Placentrex biomolecules.

Global growth projected to see slight deceleration to 3.1% in CY2026 and 3.2% in CY2027. Higher trade barriers, geopolitical disruptions and elevated inflation may increase procurement, freight, energy and compliance-related costs, while affecting delivery schedules and working-capital requirements.

Albert David Limited will continue to focus on strengthening its core business, improving operational efficiency and building a more resilient product and market portfolio. Strategic priorities include expanding market reach, strengthening existing brands, developing selected new product categories and improving engagement with healthcare professionals, institutional customers and other stakeholders.

The Company will continue to place emphasis on quality, compliance and manufacturing excellence, particularly in view of evolving domestic and international regulatory expectations. Continued focus on Revised Schedule-M compliance, process improvement and technology-led efficiency will remain important for sustaining competitiveness.

The Company intends to strengthen its digital initiatives across business processes, including better use of technology in operations, reporting, people management and internal controls, expected to support faster decision-making, improved process discipline and better organisational agility.

Material costs: Supply chain challenges and elevated raw material or resource costs could adversely impact availability and overall product cost structure, resulting in diminished margins
Geopolitical risks: Disruption could impact global supply chains, significantly straining business-as-usual operations
Climate change: Pharmaceutical industry under intense scrutiny due to high carbon footprint; risks categorised into Physical Risks and Transition Risks

Increasing competition: Intense pressure from both large-scale generic leaders and agile niche competitors; competitors aggressively slashing prices in LVP (Large Volume Parenterals) and IV fluid segments
Currency fluctuations: Unprecedented swings in foreign exchange rates driven by global geopolitical crisis may create short-term margin pressures
Regulatory approach: All regulatory authorities looking for risk-based approach in Pharma Industry
Revenue recognition risk due to estimation of discounts, incentives and rebates
Litigations and claims relating to direct, indirect tax and other matters pending with statutory authorities
Recognition of Deferred Tax Assets depends on assessment of probability of future taxable income and legal/economic limits
Right-of-use assets and lease liability require judgement in determining lease term and incremental borrowing rate
Defined Benefit Obligation measured on actuarial assumptions (mortality, withdrawal rates, discount rates, medical cost trends, salary increases, inflation) - changes may have material impact
Provisions and Contingencies evaluation based on management's best judgment regarding probability of exposure to potential loss
Impairment of Financial Assets reviewed annually or more frequently when indication of impairment exists
Allowances for Doubtful Debts require judgment and estimates - differences from original estimates impact carrying value and expenses
Fair value measurement of financial instruments requires judgement in establishing fair values when quoted prices not available, including considerations of liquidity risk, credit risk and volatility
Sales Return allowance based on estimate of expected sales returns using historical experience
Interest Rate Risk: The Defined Benefit Obligation calculation uses a discount rate based on government bonds. If bonds yield fall the defined benefit obligation will increase.

Salary Growth Risk: The present value of defined benefit plan liability is calculated by reference to the future salaries of plan participants. An increase in the salary of plan participants will increase the plan liabilities.
Demographic Risk: This is the risk of variability of results due to unsystematic nature of variables that include mortality, withdrawal, disability and retirement.
Credit Risk: The credit risk is the risk of financial loss arising from counter party failing to discharge an obligation.

Liquidity Risk: The Company determines its liquidity requirement in the short, medium and long term and manages it through ensuring operational cash flow while maintaining adequate cash and cash equivalent position.
Foreign Exchange Risk from imports of raw materials and foreign currency borrowings
Interest Rate Risk on surplus funds parked in mutual funds (debt oriented) and bonds
Other Price Risk from equity oriented mutual fund investments
Impact of New Labour Codes effective 21 November 2025
